Justice Inder Singh Mehta, President.
O R D E R :
-
The instant appeals are arising out of the

common order dated 20.02.2020 passed by learned District

Commission, Una in consumer complaint No.54/2020 titled

Pankaj Gupta & Ors. Versus Goibibo & Ors., whereby the

complaint filed by the complainant was allowed and the

opposite party No.1 was directed to refund Rs.49,107/- to

the complainant alongwith 9% interest from the date of filing

of complaint till realization. The opposite party No.1 was

further directed to pay compensation to the tune of

Rs.20,000/- on account of harassment and mental tension

and litigation cost of Rs.15,000/- to the complainant. The

opposite party No.1 was further directed to credit a Gocash
4
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

balance in the wallet of complainants to the tune of

Rs.50,000/- valid for three years on account of breach of

contract as promised and punitive compensation together.

The opposite party No.3 was directed to refund the deficient

amount of tickets to the tune of Rs.22,760/- to the

complainants.
Brief facts of the Case:
2. The brief facts of the case are that the

complainants had booked a flight from Delhi to Goa for

20.03.2020 operated by Opposite Party No.2, SpiceJet and

also booked a return flight from Goa to Delhi for 25.03.2020 by

IndiGo Airlines, operated by Opposite Party No.3, through

Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo. The bookings were confirmed on

19.01.2020. Thereafter, the flight from Delhi to Goa scheduled

for 20.03.2020 was cancelled by the airline, and an e-mail

dated 19.03.2020 to this effect was received by the

complainants. They were given an option either to reschedule

the flight or to opt for a full refund, and the complainants opted

for a full refund. On 23.03.2020, an e-mail was received from
5
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

opposite party No.2/SpiceJet informing the complainants that

refunds of Rs.24,789/-, Rs.3,963/- and Rs.8,192/-, totaling

Rs.36,944/-, had been processed through Opposite Party

No.1/Goibibo. Subsequently, on 06.06.2020, another e-mail

was received by complainant No.1 from Opposite Party

No.2/SpiceJet stating that the refund in respect of certain

bookings had been processed and advised the complainants

to contact Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo. When the

complainants contacted Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo, the

opposite party No.1 sent an e-mail stating that the refund

would be issued and, in case of delay in processing the

refund, GoCash Plus @ Rs.100/- per hour would be provided.
However, no refund was made to them. The return flight from

Goa to Delhi scheduled for 25.03.2020 was also subsequently

cancelled due to the lockdown imposed by the Central

Government on account of the outbreak of the Covid-19

pandemic. Complainant Nos.2 and 4 to 9 received partial

refunds; however, complainant Nos.1 and 3 did not receive the

refund. The complainants alleged that the failure to refund the
6
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

amount constituted deficiency in service on the part of the

opposite parties and, as such, filed the present complaint.
3. Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo filed reply and

admitted that the complainants had booked flights through

Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo from Delhi to Goa on 20.03.2020

and from Goa to Delhi on 25.03.2020 with different airlines. At

the time of booking the tickets, the travelers had duly accepted

the applicable terms and conditions. The confirmed flight

bookings were cancelled by the concerned airlines due to the

outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic and that the situation was

covered by the force majeure clause. Therefore, Opposite

Party No.1/Goibibo could not be held liable for the cancellation

of the air tickets. Reliance was also placed upon the judgment

dated 01.10.2020 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Parvasi Legal Cell v. Union of India & Others
, and it was

contended that the opposite parties had acted in accordance

with the directions issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and

the guidelines of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation

(DGCA). It was further submitted that the refund had been
7
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

processed in the Goibibo wallet of the complainants after

deduction of applicable charges. Accordingly, dismissal of the

complaint was prayed for.
4. Opposite Party No.2/SpiceJet did not appear

before the learned District Commission despite service and

was proceeded ex parte vide order dated 07.11.2020.
5. Opposite Party No.3/InterGlobe Aviation Ltd. filed

a separate reply, stating that it had duly refunded the booking

amount into the account from which the payment had been

made, i.e. the account of Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo, on

08.07.2020. It was submitted that an amount of Rs.10,614/-

had been paid by Opposite Party No.3 to Opposite Party No.1

on 08.07.2020. Since the complainants had made the booking

through Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo, the complainants were

not entitled to claim the said amount directly from Opposite

Party No.3. A prayer for dismissal of the complaint was made.
6. The complainants filed rejoinders to the replies

and denied the allegations made in the replies and the

averments of complaint were re-affirmed and reasserted.
8
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)
7. Thereafter, the parties led evidence in support

of their respective pleadings.
8. After hearing the learned counsel of the parties,

learned District Commission allowed the complaint of the

complainants.
9. Feeling dissatisfied and aggrieved by the order of

learned District Commission, the complainants and opposite

party No.1/Goibibo filed these two separate appeals.
10. Arguments heard on behalf of the parties and

perused the record of the case file carefully.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant/Goibibo

submitted that the respondents/complainants had booked

flight tickets of SpiceJet and IndiGo Airlines through the

appellant/Goibibo, which were subsequently cancelled due

to the Covid-19 pandemic and the lockdown imposed in the

country. It was submitted that the appellant-company could

not process the refund directly into the bank accounts of the

complainants; however, the ticket amount was transferred to
9
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

the Goibibo Wallet in accordance with the directions and

guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the

DGCA. He has further submitted that notice to this effect

had also been issued to the complainants through e-mail

(Annexure A-10). He has further submitted that the amount

lying in the wallet had subsequently been transferred to the

account of the complainants. He has further submitted that

here was no fault on the part of the appellant-company and

the direction to pay Rs.50,000/- on account of the alleged

breach of promise was unjustified. He prays that appeal of

the appellant company be allowed and the appeal of the

complainants be dismissed.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing

on behalf of the complainants/appellants in Appeal

No.52/2021 submitted that the complainants had booked

SpiceJet flight tickets from Delhi to Goa for 20.03.2020 and

return tickets by IndiGo Airlines from Goa to Delhi for

25.03.2020 through appellant/Goibibo. The bookings were
10
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

confirmed on 19.01.2020. It was further submitted that the

Delhi-Goa flight was cancelled by the airline and the

complainants opted for a full refund. Thereafter, an e-mail

was received from SpiceJet informing them that refunds of

Rs.24,789/-, Rs.3,963/- and Rs.8,192/-, totaling Rs.36,944/-,

had been issued to Goibibo. However, despite receipt of the

said amount, Goibibo failed to refund the same to the

complainants. He has further submitted that Goibibo had

itself promised that, in case the refund was not processed

within the stipulated time, GoCash Plus @ Rs.100/- per hour

of delay would be provided. However, neither the refund nor

the promised amount was paid within the stipulated period.

He has further submitted that the compensation awarded by

the learned District Commission was inadequate and that

the complainants were entitled to Rs.4,41,600/- towards the

delayed refund and Rs.9,00,000/- towards compensation for

mental harassment. He prays that appeal of the
11
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

complainants be allowed and appeal of the Goibibo be

dismissed.
13. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of

Opposite Party No.3/IndiGo Airlines submitted that Opposite

Party No.3 had already complied with the order passed by

the learned District Commission by paying the amount

awarded against it and that the complainants had received

the said amount without protest. It was, therefore, submitted

that nothing remained payable by Opposite Party No.3 and

the appeal against it deserves to be dismissed.

FINDINGS:
14. The admitted fact emerging on the record is that

the complainants had booked a flight by SpiceJet from Delhi

to Goa for 20.03.2020 and return tickets by IndiGo Airlines

from Goa to Delhi for 25.03.2020 through appellant/

Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo by making an online payment

of Rs.57,498/-. The bookings were confirmed on

19.01.2020.
12
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)
15. It is further an admitted fact emerging on record

that on 19.03.2020, the complainants received an e-mail

(Annexure C-1) from Opposite Party No.2/SpiceJet

informing them that Flight No. SG-8144, scheduled for

20.03.2020 from Delhi to Goa, had been cancelled. The

complainants were given an option either to reschedule the

flight or to opt for a full refund, and they opted for a refund of

the booking amount.
16. It is also not in dispute that the return flight from

Goa to Delhi scheduled for 25.03.2020, booked through

Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo with Opposite Party No.3/

IndiGo Airlines, was subsequently cancelled due to the

lockdown imposed in the country on account of the Covid-19

pandemic.
17. The grievance of the complainants is that,

despite cancellation of the flights, they did not receive the

full refund of the amounts paid by them. It has further been

alleged that Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo deducted certain
13
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

charges and, instead of refunding the amount to the

complainants, credited the same to the GoCash wallet

maintained by Goibibo.
18. On the other hand, the appellant/Goibibo has

contended that the flights were cancelled by the concerned

airlines on account of the Covid-19 pandemic and the

lockdown. The appellant-company was merely an

intermediary/booking agent. The refund amount was

credited to the GoCash wallet of the complainants in

accordance with the directions issued by the Hon'ble

Supreme Court and the guidelines of the DGCA and,

therefore, there was no deficiency in service on their part.
19. The bookings were admittedly made through

appellant/Goibibo and the payments made by the

complainants were received and processed through the

appellant-company. Once the refundable amount was

received by the appellant-company from the concerned

airline, the appellant-company was under legal obligation to
14
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

ensure that the refundable amount was duly transmitted to

the complainants within a reasonable period.
20. The record further shows that Opposite Party

No.2/SpiceJet informed the complainants that refund

amounts of Rs.24,789/-, Rs.3,963/- and Rs.8,192/-, totaling

Rs.36,944/-, had been processed/issued through

appellant/Goibibo. However, the appellant-company has

failed to establish by cogent and convincing evidence that

the said amount was actually refunded to the complainants

in their bank account within a reasonable period.
21. The plea of the appellant that the amount was

credited to the GoCash wallet of the complainants does not,

by itself, amount to valid discharge of its legal obligation to

refund the amount. The complainants had made the

payment through online mode, and there is no material on

record to establish that they had voluntarily opted to accept

the refund amount in Gocash wallet. Therefore, the
15
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

appellant-company cannot escape from its liability merely by

relying upon the credit of the amount in the GoCash wallet.
22. The reliance placed by learned counsel for the

appellant upon the judgment dated 01.10.2020 passed by

the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Parvasi Legal Cell v. Union of

India & Others
does not, in the facts and circumstances of

the present case, completely absolve the appellant from its

obligation towards the complainants. The directions issued

by the Hon'ble Supreme Court were intended to facilitate

and regulate refunds of air ticket amounts during the

exceptional situation arising out of the Covid-19 pandemic.

However, once the refund amount had been received by the

appellant-company from the concerned airline, the

appellant-company was required to deal with the said

amount in accordance with the applicable directions and to

ensure that the complainants received the refund within the

permissible period.
16
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)
23. The contention of the appellant/Goibibo that the

entire amount had already been transferred to the

complainants' account is also not established by cogent and

convincing evidence. As per Annexure C-10, relating to the

GoCash account, an amount of Rs.41,993/- was lying in the

said account, whereas the complainants had paid

Rs.57,498/- towards the booking of the flights through the

appellant-company. Thus, the appellant-company has failed

to establish that the entire refundable amount had been paid

to the complainants. The failure to refund the entire amount

constitutes deficiency in service on the part of the appellant-

company.
24. The appellant-company has further contended

that there was no breach of contract on its part and that the

delay in refunding the booking amount was attributable to

the airlines. Therefore, the appellant/Goibibo could not be

held liable to pay Rs.50,000/- towards GoCash Plus.
17
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)
25. Perusal of the e-mail (Annexure C-5) sent by

appellant/Goibibo shows that the appellant-company had

itself promised that, in case of failure to refund the amount

within the stipulated time, GoCash Plus @ Rs.100/- per hour

of delay would be provided. Further, as per Annexure C-2,

Opposite Party No.2/SpiceJet had refunded an amount of

Rs.36,944/- to the appellant-company on 23.03.2020.

However, there is no satisfactory evidence on record to

establish that the said amount was thereafter immediately

transferred to the complainants.
26. Thus, there was a failure on the part of the

appellant-company to honour the promise made by it. The

learned District Commission, therefore, was justified in

taking the said circumstance into consideration while

awarding Rs.50,000/- to the complainants. Therefore, no

interference is required in the same.
27. So far as the liability of Opposite Party

No.3/IndiGo Airlines is concerned, the said opposite party
18
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

has contended that it had already complied with the order of

the learned District Commission by refunding the amount

awarded against it. However, there is no sufficient material

or any receipt on record to establish that the entire amount

awarded against it has been paid to the complainants.

Therefore, the aforesaid plea of the opposite party

No.3/IndiGo Airlines does not seem to be correct and loose

its significance.
28. The complainants, in their appeal, have sought

enhancement of the amount payable by the appellant-

company on the ground that it had failed to refund the

booking amount within the stipulated period. It has been

alleged that the appellant-company was liable to pay

GoCash Plus @ Rs.100/- per hour from 24.03.2020 till

24.09.2020, which, according to the complainants, comes to

Rs.4,41,600/-.
29. However, the amount claimed by the

complainants on the basis of Rs.100/- per hour is highly
19
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

excessive and disproportionate. The learned District

Commission, after considering the facts and circumstances

of the case, has awarded Rs.50,000/- on account of the

breach of the promise made by the appellant-company. The

said amount appears to be just, fair and reasonable in the

facts and circumstances of the present case. No ground is

made out for further enhancement.
30. Consequently, both the appeals, i.e. the appeal

filed by appellant/Opposite Party No.1/Goibibo as well as

the appeal filed by the complainants seeking enhancement

of the amount awarded by the learned District Commission,

are found to be devoid of merit and are accordingly

dismissed and the impugned order passed by learned

District Commission remains upheld.
31. Parties are left to bear their own costs.
32. Certified copy of order be transmitted to parties

and their counsel free of costs strictly as per rules. File of

learned District Commission below alongwith certified copy
20
(F.A.No.21/2022 & F.A.No.52/2021)

of order be sent back and file of State Commission be

consigned to record room after due completion forthwith.

Certified copy of this order be also placed on the connected

appeal. The appeals are disposed of. Pending application(s)

if any also disposed of.
Justice Inder Singh Mehta
